t: The leading Welsh kingdom, based on the mountains of Snowdonia and the grain lands of Anglesey, with its chief royal court at Aberffraw.
Its rulers, from Rhodri the Great to Llywelyn the Great, repeatedly brought much of Wales under their authority.
Llywelyn ap Gruffudd was recognised as Prince of Wales in 1267, but Edward I conquered Gwynedd in 1282–1283.
dyk: A sixth-century gravestone at Penmachno calls the dead man a citizen of ‘Venedotis’, one of the earliest written records of the name of Gwynedd.
ev: Maelgwn Gwynedd, the king Gildas called the dragon of the island, dies of plague
Cadwallon ap Cadfan and Penda of Mercia defeat and kill Edwin of Northumbria
Rhodri the Great adds Powys to Gwynedd
Henry II’s invasion of Wales founders on the Berwyn mountains against Owain Gwynedd
The Treaty of Worcester confirms Llywelyn the Great’s dominance in Wales
The Treaty of Montgomery recognises Llywelyn ap Gruffudd as Prince of Wales
Llywelyn ap Gruffudd is killed near Cilmeri
The Statute of Rhuddlan turns Gwynedd into English shires
